page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a nominal base clock speed of 2.7 GHz with dedicated CPU allocation.

The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included. Local storage is not provided, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for networking.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, this configuration targets compute-dense execution rather than memory-heavy footprints. The absence of local solid-state drives necessitates external I/O considerations, making it effective for stateless processing, continuous integration agents, microservices hosting, and distributed compute nodes where cost efficiency stems from tailored compute allocation without unneeded memory overhead.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.8-32 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores mapped to 16 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring persistent data to be hosted on remote block volumes. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the hardware balance prioritizes processing capacity over large memory allocations, the instance provides cost-effective throughput for stateless backend services, software build nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed compute workloads that do not demand extensive in-memory caches or ultra-low-latency local disk arrays.
